content_text: HPCL operates its vigilance mechanism in alignment with the guidelines issued by the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) for public sector enterprises, along with directives from the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) and the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoP&NG). The Vigilance Department is headed by the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO), who is responsible for supervising and managing all vigilance-related matters within the Corporation. The department primarily addresses concerns related to corruption and other issues deemed to have a vigilance angle. Complaint handling is governed by the CVC's Vigilance Manual 2021, which is publicly available on the HPCL website: https://www. hindustanpetroleum.com/pages/ vigilance. Only complaints containing verifiable facts are investigated; anonymous, vague, or pseudonymous complaints are not pursued. In FY 2024-25, a total of 855 complaints were disposed of, while 15 complaints remained pending as of March 31, 2025. These primarily related to retail outlet and LPG distributorship selection and operations, tendering, transportation, and depot/plant operations. Alongside investigations, the department also undertakes preventive vigilance initiatives aimed at strengthening transparency and accountability in business decision-making. Vigilance activities are subject to regular review by both the CVC and the vigilance wing of the MoP&NG. The department also focuses on systemic improvements and, in FY 2024-25, proposed 44 such enhancements to management for strengthening internal controls.

HPCL's Procurement Manual governs all procurement-related activities and incorporates anti-corruption protocols based on the Government of India's General Financial Rules (GFR). All tenders and agreements include anticorruption clauses, and for contracts worth H 1 Crore and above, an Integrity Pact is incorporated in accordance with CVC directives. During the procurement and contract phases, vendors and business partners are bound by these anti-corruption commitments. Any breaches may result in termination or non-renewal of contracts.

All HPCL locations under the j urisdiction of the CVO have undergone assessments for corruption-related risks. The Company's anti-corruption policies and procedures are communicated across all governance levels and to employees. Common corruption risks include: - ~ Misuse of official position - ~ Providing undue benefit to ineligible candidates - ~ Demanding and / or accepting gratification other than legal remuneration - ~ Cases of misappropriation/ forgery/ cheating etc. - ~ Any undue/unjustified delay in the disposal of matters - ~ Gross or wilful negligence - ~ recklessness in decision making - ~ blatant violations of systems and procedures - ~ exercise of discretion in excess, where no ostensible public interest is evident - ~ failure to keep the controlling authority/superiors informed of required transactions and issues in time - ~ Cause of undue l oss or a concomitant gain to an individual or a set of individuals /party or parties / Others

The Right to Information Act, 2005 (RTI), effective from 12 October 2005, allows Indian citizens to seek information from public authorities. content_text: In FY 2024-25, HPCL achieved landmark operational milestones in its refining business. Through proactive planning, effective risk management, and informed decision-making, the Company recorded its highestever crude throughput of 25.27 Million metric tonnes (MMT), surpassing the previous record of 22.33 MMT in FY 2023-24. Both the Mumbai and Visakhapatnam refineries operated above their design capacities, achieving an average capacity utilisation of 109%, despite scheduled turnarounds. The Visakhapatnam Refinery achieved its highest annual crude throughput of 15.31 MMT, while the Mumbai Refinery processed 9.96 MMT, also a record. This robust performance was supported by enhanced refinery reliability and standardised operating procedures, enabling HPCL to achieve its highest-ever production of MS, HSD, LPG, ATF, and Bitumen during the year. HPCL further strengthened its adaptability by processing eight new crude grades, the highest in any fiscal year, bringing the total number of grades in its crude basket to 178 from regions such as West Africa, Middle East, North America, South America, Mediterranean, North Sea, Far East, Russia and India. energy such as wind and solar power. Its operations and supply chain practices integrate energy efficiency, carbon mitigation, and digital technologies to enhance resilience, reduce emissions, and create value for all stakeholders. As India transitions towards a low-carbon future, HPCL remains focused on contributing to national energy security, sustainable industrialisation, and inclusive development, in line with its mission of 'Delivering Happiness' and building a greener, self-reliant, and prosperous India. To meet India's rising energy demand and enhance energy security, HPCL has been modernising and expanding its refining infrastructure. The Visakh Refinery Modernisation Project (VRMP) has successfully commissioned several units, contributing to higher product availability and regional energy security. A major achievement includes the mechanical completion of India's first Residue Upgradation Facility (RUF) with a capacity of 3.55 MMTPA at Visakh Refinery, now in the advanced stages of commissioning. This unit, based on LC-MAX technology, will be the world's first of its kind and one of the most energy-efficient residue hydrocracker units globally. In Mumbai Refinery, the commissioning of parallel hydrotreating of Vacuum Gas Oil(VGO) in the Diesel Hydro Treating unit enabled increased MS production. Additionally, the Naphtha Isomerisation Unit at Visakh Refinery is being revamped to enhance capacity and RON. As part of its strategic focus on expanding valueadded products, Mumbai Refinery has successfully demonstrated the production of De-Aromatised

Kerosene (DAK) solvents using the HPCL Green R&D Centre (HPGRDC) HP-DAK Technology. In line with its commitment to sustainability and innovation, the refinery is also implementing a project to produce environmentally friendly Rubber Process Oil (RPO) through HPGRDC's developed Treated Distillate Aromatic Extract (TDAE) technology. Additionally, a dedicated project to produce pharmaceutical-grade Hexane is currently under implementation at the Refinery. To cater to petrochemical demand, HPCL, through its joint venture HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL), is constructing India's first integrated grassroots Refinerycum-Petrochemical Complex at Pachpadra, Rajasthan. With a Petrochemical I ntensity I ndex of 26%, the highest in India, the complex is progressing steadily, with phased commissioning expected in FY 2025-26. HPCL refineries have unlocked substantial energy savings and reduced emissions by adopting strategies such as process optimisation, advanced controls, energy recovery, equipment upgrades, renewable energy integration, and employee engagement. In FY 202425, Energy Conservation Schemes (including sustenance of previous schemes) resulted in savings of 1,56,022 SRFT/year, translating to a reduction of approximately 0.50 MMT of CO2 emissions annually.
